Amr b. Abasa met the Prophet hiding in Mecca, later joined him in Medina and learned when to pray or refrain, and how ablution and prayer wash away sins.
Aisha said the Prophet never left two rak'ahs after Asr in her house; he told Umm Salama they made up the two after noon, missed while receiving a delegation.
People prayed two rak'ahs between the sunset call and Maghrib prayer, which the Prophet saw but neither ordered nor forbade; between adhan and iqamah is a prayer for whoever wishes.
In danger the Prophet led two groups or rows that took turns praying and facing the enemy; at Dhat ar-Riqa' he prayed four rak'ahs and each group two.
Whoever comes to the Friday prayer should bathe, use siwak and perfume; Umar rebuked a latecomer who only made ablution, and the earliest comer is like one sacrificing a camel.
Telling a companion to be quiet while the Imam delivers the Friday sermon is itself idle talk.
On Friday there is a short time when Allah grants any good a Muslim asks in prayer, placed by one report between the Imam sitting down and the prayer's end.
Friday, the best day, is when Adam was created and the Hour will come; Allah guided this last community to it, while the Jews took Saturday and the Christians Sunday.
Angels at the mosque doors record Friday arrivals in order, as if sacrificing a camel down to an egg; whoever listens silently is forgiven till next Friday, plus three days.
The Prophet led the Friday prayer when the sun had passed the meridian; afterwards people rested their camels and took their siesta and lunch, finding little shade from the walls.
The Prophet delivered two Friday sermons standing, sitting between them, reciting the Quran and exhorting people; Jabir b. Samura called anyone claiming he preached sitting a liar.
When a caravan came during the Friday sermon, all but twelve left the Prophet standing and a verse came down about it, which Ka'b cited against a seated preacher.
From his pulpit the Prophet warned that people must stop neglecting the Friday prayer, or Allah will seal their hearts and they will be among the negligent.
The Prophet's prayer and sermon were moderate; preaching, his eyes reddened and voice rose like one warning of an enemy, calling Allah's Book the best speech and every innovation error.
Dimad came to Mecca to cure the Prophet of a supposed spell, heard his words of praise and testimony, and pledged allegiance on Islam for himself and his people.
Ammar said a long prayer and short sermon show understanding, as the Prophet taught; the Prophet called a preacher who said 'whoever disobeys both of them' a bad speaker.
On the pulpit the Prophet recited the Quran, including Surah Qaf every Friday, and gestured only with his forefinger, as Umara reminded Bishr b. Marwan, who raised his hands.
Whoever arrives while the Imam is preaching should pray two short rak'ahs, as the Prophet told Sulaik Ghatafani; once he left his sermon to teach a stranger the religion.
In the Friday prayer the Prophet recited al-Jumu'a and al-Munafiqun, or al-A'la and al-Ghashiya as on the Eids, and in Friday's dawn prayer al-Sajda and al-Insan.
After the Friday prayer the Prophet prayed two rak'ahs at home and told people to pray four, without joining it to another prayer before talking or going out.
The Prophet, Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthman prayed Eid before the sermon, without adhan or iqamah; the Prophet then urged the women to give alms, and they gave rings.
The Prophet commanded that young, secluded and menstruating women be brought out for the two Eids, the menstruating staying away from the prayer place but joining the supplication.
On Eid the Prophet prayed two rak'ahs, nothing before or after, and told the women to give alms; in Eid prayers he recited Qaf and 'The Hour drew near'.
On Eid the Prophet stopped Abu Bakr scolding two girls singing and drumming, saying every people has a festival, and let Aisha watch Abyssinians play with spears in the mosque.
Praying for rain at the prayer place, the Prophet faced the Qibla, turned his mantle round and prayed two rak'ahs, raising his hands so high his armpits showed.
Asked during the Friday sermon, the Prophet prayed for rain and it rained a week; asked again, he prayed it fall around Medina, not on it, and it cleared.
The Prophet let rain fresh from his Lord touch his body, but feared storm wind and dark clouds might be a calamity, like the wind that destroyed 'Ad.
In the eclipse prayer the Prophet bowed twice each rak'ah, then said sun and moon are signs not eclipsed for anyone's death or birth; he had seen Paradise and Hell.
The eclipse prayer, called in congregation and recited aloud, had two rak'ahs of two or three bowings each and four prostrations, with remembrance of Allah till the sun cleared.
After a Jewess spoke of the grave's torment, the Prophet led an eclipse prayer, then said people are tried in graves like the Dajjal's turmoil, and sought refuge from it.
Praying during eclipses, one on the day Ibrahim died, the Prophet was shown Paradise and Hell, where a woman suffered for starving a cat and a man dragged his intestines.
After the eclipse prayer, Asma' heard the Prophet say people will be tried in their graves and asked about him, the believer affirming him, the hypocrite not knowing.
Perturbed by an eclipse, the Prophet took a woman's garment by mistake, then stood so long that Asma' wished to sit and a newcomer would think he had not bowed.
After a long eclipse prayer the Prophet said he reached for grapes in Paradise and saw Hell, most of its people women, for their ingratitude to husbands and to kindness.
Ibn Abbas reported four bowings in each of the two eclipse rak'ahs and Amr b. al-As two, Aisha saying she never saw longer bowing and prostration.
Eclipses are signs by which Allah frightens His servants, not for anyone's death, as people said when Ibrahim died; on seeing one, pray, supplicate and remember Allah till it clears.
The Prophet said to prompt those who are dying to say 'There is no god but Allah'.
Whoever, hit by calamity, says 'We belong to Allah and to Him we return' is given better; Umm Salama said it when Abu Salama died and married the Prophet.
Closing the dead Abu Salama's eyes, the Prophet said sight follows the departing soul, told the family to pray only for good as angels say amen, and prayed for him.
The Prophet stopped Umm Salama's planned mourning, yet wept at his daughter's dying child and at the sick Sa'd b. Ubada, saying Allah punishes for the tongue, not tears.
